subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹20,900 on simple interest, partly at 10% per annum and partly at 9% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 8 years, then find the sum invested at 10% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When simple interests are equal for the same time period, the investments are in the inverse ratio of their rates.

Ratio of investments = P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁

⇒ P₁ : P₂ = 9 : 10

Total ratio parts = 9 + 10 = 19

Sum invested at 10% (P₁) = (9 ÷ 19) × 20900 = 9900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹20,900

Rate 1 (R₁) = 10% per annum

Rate 2 (R₂) = 9% per annum

Time (T) = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
